_readme: weeks: one theme per week, keyed by the week's SUNDAY (YYYY-MM-DD); shown as 'This week: <theme>' and in the share text. days: one entry per date (YYYY-MM-DD). side: the day's angle on the week's theme; shown small under 'This week: …' and as the 'Tomorrow:' teaser after the quiz. It must say only what the 3 verses say. verses: 1 OT then 2 NT, KJV word for word. quiz: one question per verse ('verse' is the verse index, 'answer' is the index of the right choice). commentary: null, or {text, father, work, source_url} from a Church Father before AD 451, verified in a public-domain source; shown under the verses only when filled in. See README.md. glossary: shared list of old KJV words and plain meanings; the page lists, under each verse, only the glossary words found in it.

verses.text: Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore.
Thou hast made known to me the ways of life; thou shalt make me full of joy with thy countenance.
Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.

quiz.q: In Psalm 16:11, what is in God’s presence?
In Acts 2:28, with what does God make me full of joy?
In Romans 15:13, the God of hope fills you with all joy and what?

verses.text: Therefore with joy shall ye draw water out of the wells of salvation.
And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.
And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people.

quiz.q: In Isaiah 12:3, from which wells do we draw water with joy?
In Luke 1:47, in whom does my spirit rejoice?
In Luke 2:10, what did the angel bring?

verses.text: For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.
My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations;
But rejoice, inasmuch as ye are partakers of Christ’s sufferings; that, when his glory shall be revealed, ye may be glad also with exceeding joy.

quiz.q: In Psalm 30:5, when does joy come?
In James 1:2, when should we count it all joy?
In 1 Peter 4:13, we rejoice as partakers of what?

verses.text: They that sow in tears shall reap in joy.
Verily, verily, I say unto you, That ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy.
And ye now therefore have sorrow: but I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man taketh from you.

quiz.q: In Psalm 126:5, what do they that sow in tears reap?
In John 16:20, what shall your sorrow be turned into?
In John 16:22, who can take your joy from you?

verses.text: Serve the LORD with gladness: come before his presence with singing.
How that in a great trial of affliction the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded unto the riches of their liberality.
Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.

quiz.q: In Psalm 100:2, how should we serve the LORD?
In 2 Corinthians 8:2, what did they have in a great trial of affliction?
In 2 Corinthians 9:7, what kind of giver does God love?

verses.text: Then he said unto them, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our Lord: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the LORD is your strength.
These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.
And these things write we unto you, that your joy may be full.

quiz.q: In Nehemiah 8:10, what is the joy of the LORD?
In John 15:11, what does Jesus want to remain in you?
In 1 John 1:4, what may your joy be?

verses.text: This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
Rejoice in the Lord alway: and again I say, Rejoice.
Rejoice evermore.

quiz.q: In Psalm 118:24, what will we do in the day the LORD hath made?
In Philippians 4:4, how often should we rejoice in the Lord?
In 1 Thessalonians 5:16, how long should we rejoice?
